note: The two sets are substantively identical: the same 19 claims, values, units and quotes, differing only in ordering and in that Set A adds the condition 'load of laundry' to the clothes-drying eligibility claim, which is merely the subject of that claim rather than a needed condition. Both read the Figure 8 scoring thresholds (≤100, 100–110, ≥110 % of original weight) and the dishwasher temperatures (120°F/48.9°C full, 115°F/46.1°C half) correctly and bind them to the right subcontest/component. Both sets repeat the same facts under two names (sensor count, 120°F, 115°F, and the three scoring bands stated both as 'Clothes Dryer Subcontest' and 'clothes-drying task'), so both carry the same duplication overhead. Neither set is more correct or more complete than the other.
remarks: Both sets miss several facts on the page: the temperature-of-record rule (higher of the two sensor readings, lower only if the higher-reading sensor is defective), the definition of cycle 'interruption' (8-5e), cycle completion confirmed by audible or visible signal (8-5f), the allowed load states (empty/partial/full, soiled or clean, 8-5h), the requirement to dry two loads on several days of contest week with each load scored separately (8-4d), and the requirement that towel-visible drying methods be demonstrated to the architecture and market appeal juries (8-4c). Note also that 'minimum wash and rinse cycles: 1' loosely paraphrases 'at least one wash and rinse cycle' (a single cycle containing both wash and rinse), a mild paraphrase rather than a distinct countable attribute.
